newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Strikers defy return order in Manila waterworks.
newsitem.headline: Strikers defy return order in Manila waterworks.

text.p: Workers of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) on the third day of their strike on Friday defied an order for them to return to work.
"We have defied the return-to-work order. We are still outside the MWSS compound," Elizabeth Nuyad, spokeswoman for the Alliance of MWSS Employees and Supervisors, told Reuters by telephone.
She said striking workers, whom she estimated at 5,700, would continue their walk-out until President Fidel Ramos acceded to their demand for a higher severance pay package.
MWSS supplies water and maintains the sewage system for 12 million people in Manila and its neighbouring provinces.
The walk-out has not affected the water supply in the area, and Nuyad said the strikers were not yet keen on carrying out their earlier threat to cut off water supply.
"That is not yet in our minds. We are not that desperate. We can still wait for the President's decision," Nuyad added.

On Thursday, MWSS administrator Angel Lazaro ordered the workers to return to work after the MWSS board rejected their demand saying a severance package has been signed with the concessionaires who were set to take over the water supply and sewerage agency next month.
The order said those workers who failed to go back to work would face administrative and legal sanctions. Lazaro did not specify what awaits defiant strikers.
Based on the agreement with the concessionaires, MWSS workers will be given a six-month probationary period for them to be evaluated before being absorbed into the new structure.
Those who will not be hired by the new concessionaires will be accorded a severance package equivalent to one month pay for every year of service.
The workers were demanding one-and-a-half months' pay for every year of service.
In January, the government auctioned two 25-year concessions to operate the east and west areas of Manila.

A consortium of Ayala Corp, Bechtel Corp of the United States and United Utilities won the contract for the east zone of Manila. The west zone was won by Benpres Holdings Corp and Lyonnaise des Eaux SA.
